library_preparation_preflight.summary: Two required dependencies of hibernate-memcached 1.3 have no jars on Maven Central, so Gradle can't resolve the library as published. spy:spymemcached:2.7.1 has no Central artifact at all, and hibernate 3.2.6.ga pulls in javax.transaction:jta:1.0.1B, which has a POM but no jar. Both need to be excluded and replaced with versions that are on Central. A memcached server isn't needed: the library's own reflection runs without one.

Replaces javax.transaction:jta:1.0.1B, a compile dependency of org.hibernate:hibernate:3.2.6.ga. Central has its POM but not its jar, so resolution fails. Existing tests already use the same replacement (tests/src/net.sf.ehcache/ehcache-core/2.4.4).

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance:
Build file: declare the library with exclusions, the same way tests/src/com.google.inject.extensions/guice-servlet/4.0/build.gradle does: testImplementation("com.googlecode:hibernate-memcached:$libraryVersion") { exclude group: 'spy', module: 'spymemcached'; exclude group: 'javax.transaction', module: 'jta' }. The replacement dependencies above then fill the gaps.

Where the library uses reflection: MemcachedCacheProvider.start(Properties) calls Class.forName(...).newInstance() on the key strategy class (property hibernate.memcached.keyStrategy) and Class.forName(...).getConstructor(PropertiesHelper.class).newInstance(...) on the client factory class (property hibernate.memcached.memcacheClientFactory). Cover these by calling MemcachedCacheProvider directly with Properties, not by building a Hibernate SessionFactory. Set the key strategy to each built-in class: HashCodeKeyStrategy, Md5KeyStrategy, Sha1KeyStrategy, StringKeyStrategy. For the client factory, use the default com.googlecode.hibernate.memcached.spymemcached.SpyMemcacheClientFactory and also a test-defined public MemcacheClientFactory with a public (PropertiesHelper) constructor.

No server is needed: SpyMemcacheClientFactory builds its MemcachedClient against hibernate.memcached.servers=localhost:11211 and connects asynchronously. Cover hibernate.memcached.connectionFactory set to DefaultConnectionFactory, KetamaConnectionFactory and BinaryConnectionFactory, and hibernate.memcached.hashAlgorithm. Call provider.stop() so the client shuts down.

Test MemcachedCache logic (put/get/remove/clear, namespace keys, the dogpile prevention option, exception handling) through buildCache(region, props), backed by a test-defined in-memory Memcache implementation. Don't run cache operations against the real spymemcached client: with no server, each one waits for the operation timeout.

risks: The simple-spring-memcached spymemcached 2.7.3 jar is a third-party republish of 2.7.x. Its binary compatibility with the library comes from javap only and hasn't been run in a Gradle build yet.

spymemcached starts background I/O threads that keep trying to connect to localhost:11211 while no server runs. If the provider is left running, tests can print connection-refused logs or hang the JVM or native test at shutdown.
hibernate 3.2.6.ga uses old cglib/asm 1.5.3. Bootstrapping a full SessionFactory on JDK 25 or in Native Image will probably fail, so coverage should go through CacheProvider/Cache directly.
The DangaMemcacheClientFactory reflection (Class.forName for the error handler) stays unreachable because com.danga:java_memcached isn't on Maven Central.
